contents: Esports World Cup 2026, 2026-07-15 to 2026-07-19. 28 events trimmed to 6.
whyThisFixtureExists: rest_getSchedule.json contains no team playing under a league slug other than its own home league, so the cross-league resolution path had no evidence. The only such case in that capture was KeSPA Cup, which config/leagues.json classifies as minor and therefore never resolves. In the full 28-event response, 48 of 56 non-TBD sides resolve to a team whose homeLeague is not the Esports World Cup.

selection: index 0  SEN (LCS) vs TS (home league IS Esports World Cup) — not every team at an international event is cross-league
index 1  GEN (LCK) vs KC (LEC) — the plain cross-league case
index 7  JDG (LPL) vs LYON (LCS) — the code LYON is also claimed by an LRN org, which the major filter excludes
index 27 KC (LEC) vs DK (LCK) — Bo5 final
trimming.ordering: upstream order preserved; `pages` copied verbatim from the untrimmed response

verification.hl: verified. Sent explicitly; blockName values are English ("Groups", "Quarterfinals", "Finals").
verification.leagueId: verified. 116838530616006090 is the id of slug ewc_lol in rest_getLeagues.json. All 28 returned events carry league.slug ewc_lol.
verification.pages: verified for this response: both cursors are null, meaning ewc_lol's 28 events fit inside one 80-event page. CORRECTED 2026-08-12: this does NOT mean a leagueId call is single-page in general -- lck's leagueId call returned 80 events with pages.older non-null, a genuinely paginated result. See the leagueId section of docs/sources/lolesports-rest.md.
verification.state: All 28 events report state "completed" and every team has a result, so this capture exercises no lossy-state correction. That path stays covered by rest_getSchedule.json.

transform.why: the 6 of 28 events described in trimming.selection: one team homed at the event itself, the plain cross-league case, a three-region case, a fourth cross-league pairing, a codecollision case (LYON), and the Bo5 final.
